atoms.text: This guide describes how to give the OrbitETL batch service access to the bucket acme-analytics-lake in account 111122223333. OrbitETL runs nightly jobs that read raw CSV files under the raw/ prefix and write Parquet files under the curated/ prefix. The jobs run under the IAM role OrbitEtlRole, and the grant is made entirely in an identity-based policy attached to that role. The bucket policy of acme-analytics-lake is not modified in this procedure. In the IAM console, create a customer managed policy with an Allow statement for s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-analytics-lake/raw/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-analytics-lake/curated/*. Add a second statement that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-analytics-lake with an s3:prefix condition limited to raw/* and curated/*. Attach the policy to OrbitEtlRole. Start a test job and confirm that it lists raw/, reads one input object, and writes one output object under curated/. If the job returns AccessDenied, review the policies attached to the role and any permissions boundary that applies to it.

This guide describes how to give the OrbitETL batch service access to the bucket acme-analytics-lake in account 111122223333. OrbitETL runs nightly jobs that read raw CSV files under the raw/ prefix and write Parquet files under the curated/ prefix. The jobs run under the IAM role OrbitEtlRole, and the grant is made entirely in the bucket's resource-based policy. No permissions policy is attached to the role for this bucket. In the bucket's permissions tab, add a statement with Effect Allow and Principal set to arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/OrbitEtlRole, with s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-analytics-lake/raw/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-analytics-lake/curated/*. Add a second statement for the same principal that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-analytics-lake with an s3:prefix condition limited to raw/* and curated/*. Save the bucket policy and confirm that it validates without warnings. Start a test job and confirm that it lists raw/, reads one input object, and writes one output object under curated/. If the job returns AccessDenied, review the bucket policy statements and any explicit Deny that matches the role.

This guide covers access for the QueryLane SQL service, which stores the results of ad hoc queries in the bucket acme-query-results. QueryLane executes queries as the IAM role QueryLaneExecRole in account 444455556666. Each query result is written as a compressed file under the prefix results/ followed by the query ID. The permission is granted only through an identity-based policy on the role, and the bucket policy is left unchanged. Create an IAM policy with an Allow statement for s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-query-results/results/*. Add s3:GetBucketLocation and s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-query-results so the service can verify the output location before it runs a query. Attach the policy to QueryLaneExecRole. Run a query that returns a few rows and verify that a result file appears under results/. If the write fails, check the role's policies and look for a service control policy that blocks s3:PutObject.

Add a second statement for the same principal with s3:GetBucketLocation and s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-query-results so the service can verify the output location before it runs a query. Save the bucket policy. Run a query that returns a few rows and verify that a result file appears under results/. If the write fails, check the bucket policy and look for an explicit Deny statement that matches the role.

This procedure gives the LogPrism log analytics service access to the bucket acme-access-logs. LogPrism reads gzip-compressed web server logs from the prefix weblogs/ and writes hourly aggregate reports to the prefix reports/hourly/. The service runs as the IAM role LogPrismWorker in account 777788889999. The grant is expressed in an identity-based policy attached to LogPrismWorker, and the bucket policy is not edited. The policy contains an Allow statement for s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-access-logs/weblogs/* and a second statement for s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-access-logs/reports/hourly/*. It also allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition of weblogs/ and reports/hourly/. After attaching the policy, trigger a manual aggregation for a single hour. Verify that the report object is created and that its size is nonzero. If the job cannot read the logs, confirm that the role is the one the service actually assumes and that its attached policies include the statements above.

The service runs as the IAM role LogPrismWorker in account 777788889999. The grant is expressed in the bucket's resource-based policy, and the role has no identity-based policy for this bucket. The bucket policy contains an Allow statement with Principal set to arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/LogPrismWorker for s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-access-logs/weblogs/* and a second statement for s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-access-logs/reports/hourly/*. It also allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket for that principal with a prefix condition of weblogs/ and reports/hourly/. After saving the bucket policy, trigger a manual aggregation for a single hour. Verify that the report object is created and that its size is nonzero. If the job cannot read the logs, confirm that the role ARN in the Principal element matches the role the service actually assumes.

This guide explains how to let the TelemetryRoll service process device readings stored in the bucket acme-iot-readings. TelemetryRoll reads raw JSON files from the prefix incoming/ and writes daily rollup files to the prefix rollups/daily/. It authenticates as the IAM user telemetryroll-svc in account 222233334444, which uses long-term access keys. The access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to that user, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a policy that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-iot-readings/incoming/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-iot-readings/rollups/daily/*. Include s3:ListBucket on the bucket restricted to those two prefixes. Attach the policy to telemetryroll-svc, either directly or through a group. Run the rollup for one day of data and check that exactly one output file is written per device group. If the run fails with AccessDenied, verify the policy attachment and confirm that the access key in use belongs to this user.

This guide configures access for the SegmentCompact service, which merges many small event files into larger ones in the bucket acme-event-store. SegmentCompact reads files under the prefix events/staging/ and writes merged files under the prefix events/compacted/. The service assumes the IAM role SegmentCompactRole in account 555566667777. The grant is carried only by an identity-based policy on that role, and the bucket policy remains as it is. The policy allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-event-store/events/staging/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-event-store/events/compacted/*. It also allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket for the two prefixes and s3:DeleteObject on the staging prefix, because the service removes source files after a successful merge. Attach the policy to SegmentCompactRole and run a compaction on a single partition. Confirm that the merged file exists and that the source files are removed. If deletion fails, check that the role policy includes s3:DeleteObject for the staging prefix.

This guide sets up the LedgerSheet reporting service so that it can read sales exports and write finished reports in the bucket acme-finance-data. LedgerSheet reads CSV exports from the prefix exports/sales/ and writes monthly summary files to the prefix reports/monthly/. It runs as the IAM role LedgerSheetRole in account 888899990000. The grant is made in an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is not modified. Create a policy with s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-finance-data/exports/sales/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-finance-data/reports/monthly/*. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a condition on the s3:prefix key for exports/sales/ and reports/monthly/. Attach the policy to LedgerSheetRole. Generate a report for the previous month and confirm that the summary file appears with the expected row count. If the report is not written, check that no permissions boundary on the role excludes s3:PutObject.

LedgerSheet reads CSV exports from the prefix exports/sales/ and writes monthly summary files to the prefix reports/monthly/. It runs as the IAM role LedgerSheetRole in account 888899990000. The grant is made in the bucket's resource-based policy, and the role carries no identity-based policy for this bucket. Add a statement with Principal set to arn:aws:iam::888899990000:role/LedgerSheetRole and Effect Allow, with s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-finance-data/exports/sales/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-finance-data/reports/monthly/*. Add s3:ListBucket for the same principal on the bucket with a condition on the s3:prefix key for exports/sales/ and reports/monthly/. Save the bucket policy. Generate a report for the previous month and confirm that the summary file appears with the expected row count. If the report is not written, check that no Deny statement in the bucket policy matches s3:PutObject for this role.

This guide describes access for the ClickWeave sessionization tool, which reads clickstream files and writes session tables in the bucket acme-web-analytics. ClickWeave reads newline-delimited JSON from the prefix clicks/raw/ and writes session files to the prefix clicks/sessions/. It is run by a scheduler under the IAM user clickweave-batch in account 333344445555. Access is provided only by an identity-based policy attached to the user, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a managed policy that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-web-analytics/clicks/raw/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-web-analytics/clicks/sessions/*. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket limited to the clicks/ prefix. Attach the policy to clickweave-batch. Run the tool against a single hour of input and verify that session files are written with the same partition naming as the input. If the tool reports AccessDenied, list the attached policies for the user and check for a policy that denies s3:PutObject.

Add a bucket policy statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-web-analytics/clicks/raw/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-web-analytics/clicks/sessions/*, with Principal set to arn:aws:iam::333344445555:user/clickweave-batch. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket for the same principal, limited to the clicks/ prefix. Save the bucket policy. Run the tool against a single hour of input and verify that session files are written with the same partition naming as the input. This guide grants the QualityGate validation service access to the bucket acme-warehouse-staging. QualityGate reads data partitions from the prefix tables/orders/ and writes validation reports to the prefix quality-reports/. Reads and writes are kept on separate prefixes, and the service must not modify the source data. The service runs as the IAM role QualityGateRole in account 666677778888. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy on that role, and the bucket policy is not changed. The policy allows only s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-warehouse-staging/tables/orders/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-warehouse-staging/quality-reports/*. It also allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket for those two prefixes. Attach the policy to QualityGateRole and validate one partition. Confirm that a report file is created in quality-reports/ and that the source objects are unchanged. If the service attempts to write to tables/orders/, the request should fail, because the role has no s3:PutObject permission on that prefix.
